name: IL-16
label: Safe R

key_factors: Prediction markets price Democratic win at about 3%
No polling and no expert ratings on the race
model.rationale: The district's R+11 lean, LaHood's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial edge ($6.7M on hand versus $230K) leave Nolley with no visible path, and markets agree at roughly a 3% Democratic chance. With no polls or ratings to contradict the fundamentals, this sits firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: A late, well-funded outside spending blitz against LaHood or a major scandal would be the only realistic route to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Darin LaHood seeks another term in a central Illinois district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He has raised $3.7 million and holds $6.7 million in cash, dwarfing Democrat Paul Nolley's $416,000 raised and $230,000 on hand, with essentially no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets give Nolley only about a 3% chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district lean, incumbency, and money, all of which point the same way. Barring an unexpected external shock, LaHood is positioned for a comfortable win.
